subject: business-studies
title: Ratio Analysis Overview
welcome_lead: Compress whole accounts into a handful of decisive ratios.
meta_desc: A-Level Finance: liquidity, profitability, gearing and efficiency ratios.
final_note: Ratios are signals, not verdicts - always compare across years and rivals.

concepts.def: Current assets divided by current liabilities.
(Current assets minus stock) divided by current liabilities.
Operating profit divided by capital employed, expressed as a percentage.
Gross profit as a percentage of revenue.
Net profit as a percentage of revenue.
Long-term debt as a share of total capital employed.

walkthroughs.body_html: Current ratio = CA / CL. A figure around 1.5 to 2 is typical. Acid test strips out stock - for stock-heavy retailers it can dip below 1 safely.
ROCE = operating profit divided by capital employed, times 100. It shows how efficiently capital is converted into operating profit and is a key signal for investors.
Gearing = long-term liabilities divided by (capital + long-term liabilities), times 100. Above 50 percent is highly geared - interest costs can swamp profits in a downturn.

options: Current assets divided by current liabilities

mcqs.q: What does a liquidity ratio like the current ratio measure?
options: Liquidity ratios measure how quickly a business sells products.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
A business's ability to meet short-term obligations — current assets divided by current liabilities. A ratio above 1 means assets cover liabilities; too high may indicate poor use of resources.
A higher liquidity ratio is always better.

mcqs.q: How is Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) calculated?
options: ROCE is just net profit divided by revenue.
ROCE is the wages divided by hours worked.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.

Operating profit divided by capital employed (total equity + non-current liabilities), expressed as a percentage. It measures how efficiently the business uses its long-term financing to generate profit.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit?
options: Gross profit and net profit are the same thing.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Gross profit = revenue minus cost of goods sold (direct costs only); net profit = revenue minus ALL costs including overheads, interest and tax. Net profit is the bottom line.
Liquidity ratios measure how quickly a business sells products.
